- Overall throughput (tokens/sec) for our tenant has dropped ~35% despite steady incoming traffic

We've attached a small CSV (p95_report.csv) with sample timestamps and a logs bundle (logs_20270503.zip) that includes request ids and timestamps. Examples: request ids DAI-req-9a3f / DAI-req-9a8c showing p99 spikes at 12s and intermittent 502s.

Thanks,

Quick triage notes after scanning logs (high level):
- Patterns look consistent with long-window KV cache churn across multi-tenant GPU instances. When many large-context requests stream concurrently we see a spike in memory pressure and queueing. That amplifies p99.
- There's also a recent kernel-selection fallback we rolled earlier this week for some LlamaX variants that increases latency in worst-case long sequences; this aligns with the timeline.

Immediate mitigations we can do from server-side (fast):
1) Enable per-tenant prefix caching for DeepAssist (reduces repeated KV work). This is a config flip and can be applied within ~20-30 mins for the tenant.
2) Route DeepAssist's 32k requests to the "rwd-medium-32k-fast" variant (different kernel selection, slightly higher cost but much lower tail latency). Rolling this can be done in 45-60 mins with grace period.
3) As a last resort, apply a transient request-shed policy for the most expensive 32k-open requests (throttle to protect overall throughput).

Data I need from you (Samir):
- A sample request_id that hit p99 (you included a few; the specific top offenders would help)
- Whether you can test switching 5-10% of traffic to 8k to verify improvement

I'm attaching a tiny config snippet with the flip we recommend (mitigation_snippet.txt).

I'll start the tenant prefix-caching flip once you confirm.

—Ava
Staff SWE, Inference Platform
